section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the measures used in a single study comparing women (n=199) and men (n=200) on body appreciation, appearance investment, sociocultural attitudes, connectedness to nature, nature exposure, self-esteem, and BMI. The study employed the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) to assess body appreciation and self-reported BMI calculated from participant-provided height and weight. Table 1 presents descriptive statistics and between-group comparisons showing that women and men did not significantly differ on body appreciation (M=3.54 vs 3.53) or BMI (M=26.66 vs 25.58), though several other variables showed significant gender differences.
